items.basis: The proposed mechanism incorrectly assumes PID causes a forward movement of the neutral point to the positive pole, when in fact PID is primarily caused by ion migration creating shunting paths, not neutral point shift (doi:10.1155/2018/3286124)
The candidate fails to address boundary conditions for varying temperature coefficients, humidity levels, and module types that affect PID susceptibility (doi:10.3390/en12224230)
The provided evidence includes studies on reflector materials and silicon recovery that are completely unrelated to PID mitigation, demonstrating a fundamental misunderstanding of the problem domain
The candidate claims to limit annual power loss below 0.5% but provides no comparative data against existing PID mitigation techniques that already achieve similar or better results

Implementing a voltage balancing system that can accurately monitor and adjust neutral point positions across a 25-year lifespan in high-voltage strings is technologically infeasible given current power electronics reliability constraints
The testable prediction fails to specify how power degradation rates will be isolated from other environmental factors that influence module performance over extended testing periods
